scene information.what: Theo, who has been estranged from the friend group for three years after a bitter fallout over a shared business venture (Theo felt Caleb and Ivy had betrayed him by secretly selling their shares), receives a surprise knock on his apartment door. It's Caleb and Ivy, who have come to invite him to a small reunion at their old hangout spot, a billiard room they now own jointly. The living room is tense-Caleb stands awkwardly near the bookshelf, Ivy sits on the sofa with her hands clasped. Theo stands by the window, arms crossed. They avoid eye contact. Ivy breaks the silence by mentioning that Mercy (the fourth friend) has been diagnosed with a serious illness and has asked to see all of them one last time. This news stuns Theo. Caleb apologizes for past decisions, but Theo deflects, saying 'You don't get to use Mercy as a guilt trip.' The air is thick with unresolved resentment, but the invitation is left on the table-Theo doesn't say yes, but he doesn't say no. After a moment of visible hesitation, looking out the window and taking a deep breath, Theo agrees to come, but not for forgiveness.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: Theo. We knocked twice. You didn't answer.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: I was hoping you'd leave.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: Look, I know we're the last people you want to see, but I've been practicing my apology face and it's not working, so let's just skip to Mercy.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: Mercy? She hasn't spoken to me in three years. None of you have.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: She's sick. Really sick. She asked to see us all. One last time.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: Last time? What do you mean, last time?

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: It's bad, Theo. She wants the old group. The old place. Saturday.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: You don't get to use Mercy as a guilt trip.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: We know we hurt you. We were wrong. But this isn't about us.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: You sold me out. Both of you. And now you want a reunion?

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: I'm sorry. For all of it. Truly.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: She's fading, Theo. Please.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: I'll come. Not for you. Not for the past. For Mercy. But don't mistake this for forgiveness.

scene information.what: The next day, Mercy has arrived early at the reunion venue (the billiard room's adjoining kitchenette, being prepped for a small dinner). She looks frail but determined. Caleb helps her chop vegetables, trying to make small talk. Mercy stops him, saying she knows about the old business betrayal and about how Theo has been shut out. She reveals that she was the one who convinced Ivy to secretly sell the shares-not to hurt Theo, but because the company was failing and she needed the money for her mother's surgery. She never told anyone, and has carried the guilt. Caleb is shocked-he had always blamed Theo for being greedy. Mercy asks Caleb to keep this secret, but to find a way to bring Theo back into the fold. Caleb, moved by her honesty, promises to try. He hugs her, and they share a quiet moment of vulnerability. The kitchenette smells of onions and fresh bread, a stark contrast to the bitterness outside.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: You shouldn't be standing so long. Sit.

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: I need to do something useful. Before I can't.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: The onions are making me cry. Or is it the guilt?

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: Caleb. I know about the shares. All of it.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: You knew? We never told you.

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: I told Ivy to sell. Behind your back. Behind Theo's.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: You? But we blamed Theo for being greedy.

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: The company was failing. I needed cash for my mother's surgery. She died anyway.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: Why didn't you say anything? All these years?

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: Shame. And I didn't want to break the group more than I already had.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: You broke us, Mercy. But you're fixing us now.

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: Tell Theo. Not Ivy. She'd never forgive herself.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: I'll be the bridge. I swear.

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: Thank you. The bread is almost done. It smells like home.

scene information.what: The reunion takes place at the billiard room-the same place where they used to spend weekends. Theo arrives last, looking nervous. The four stand around the green felt table, drinks in hand. Mercy, leaning on a stool with a blanket, smiles faintly. Ivy breaks the ice by putting a cue stick in Theo's hand and saying 'No hard feelings, just a game.' Theo reluctantly plays a few shots. Mid-game, Mercy coughs, and the mood shifts. Theo asks Mercy directly why she wanted this reunion. Mercy looks at Caleb, who nods. Mercy then confesses the truth about the shares-she takes full responsibility, exonerating Caleb and Ivy. Theo is stunned, then tears up. He puts the cue down, walks to Mercy, and hugs her. He then turns to Caleb and Ivy, and says, 'I'm sorry I believed the worst of you.' Ivy shows initial surprise, but then they all embrace, and for the first time in years, the laughter returns as they play a sloppy, forgiving game of pool, including a moment where Theo misses a shot and they all laugh. The sub-text is about letting go of blame and choosing friendship over pride.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: You came. I didn't think you would.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: I said I would. I keep my word.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: Here. No hard feelings. Just a game.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: You always break first. Remember?

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: I remember everything. That's the problem.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: Why did you really want this, Mercy?

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: Because I owe you the truth.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: Go on. I've tried to fix this with banter and bad pool shots, and it's not working. They need the truth, not my jokes. Just-go on. I'll be right here, sweating through my shirt.

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: I told Ivy to sell the shares. Not Theo. Not Caleb. Me.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: What? You?

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: You told me to sell? I thought it was my idea?

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: I needed money for my mother. The company was sinking. I chose her. I'm sorry.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: All this time, I thought... I blamed both of them.

scene.speaker: Mercy
scene.content: Blame me. Only me.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: No. I'm sorry I believed the worst of you.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: We're all sorry. Let's just play.

scene.speaker: Caleb
scene.content: To Mercy. To second chances.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: No more secrets. No more leaving. We're done running. This is us, whole again.

scene.speaker: Ivy
scene.content: Your shot, Theo. Don't miss this time.

scene.speaker: Theo
scene.content: I always miss when I'm nervous.
